# Preregistration draft: formalised argument scaffolding and separated reasoning outcomes (multi-item replication)

**Version:** 0.1 draft for internal review — freeze and hash before any data collection.
**Provenance statement (required, verbatim in the final prereg):** The calibration and dissociation hypotheses below were generated by exploratory analysis of the completed single-item Sami-father experiment (`sami_father_reasoning_v1`), in which a formalised-argumentation prompt did not improve a strict commitment-based correctness outcome (−4.17 pp, 95% CI −12.04 to +3.78) but increased solution recognition and epistemic qualification in blind-coded diagnostics. This study is the prospective test of those generated hypotheses on new items and new data.

## 1. Background and rationale

The predecessor study collapsed several constructs — solution recognition, decisive commitment, non-ambiguity, non-contradiction — into one binary outcome, on a single item whose target answer may be compatible with rather than entailed by its premises. Its exploratory diagnostics suggested a dissociation: formal scaffolding shifted responses from contradiction toward correct-but-qualified answers. This study separates the constructs, uses items whose epistemic status is independently adjudicated in advance, and treats items rather than generations as the unit of generalisation.

## 2. Hypotheses (confirmatory)

**H1 (recognition).** On items with a uniquely entailed target, the formalised-argumentation prompt increases the rate at which responses identify the target solution, relative to an answer-only prompt.

**H2 (calibration — primary).** The formalised prompt increases epistemic calibration, defined per response as: on entailed items, committing to the target without qualification; on underdetermined items, explicitly identifying underdetermination or presenting candidate answers as possibilities. Prediction: the formalised−answer-only calibration difference is positive, and the condition×item-type interaction on unqualified commitment is negative (the scaffold reduces commitment specifically where commitment is unwarranted).

**H3 (commitment cost).** On entailed items, the formalised prompt does not reduce unqualified-commitment-to-target by more than 5 percentage points (non-inferiority). This is the prospective test of whether the predecessor's commitment loss was an artefact of item underdetermination (in which case it should largely disappear on genuinely entailed items) or an intrinsic hedging tax of the scaffold.

**H4 (contradiction).** The formalised prompt reduces the rate of responses containing claims contradicting stated premises, across both item types.

H2 is the single primary hypothesis. H1, H3, H4 are secondary confirmatory hypotheses with Holm correction across the three. Everything else reported is exploratory.

## 3. Design

Two-arm comparison (answer-only vs formalised argumentation; prompts frozen and hashed, task-fact content identical between arms) crossed with item type (entailed vs underdetermined), within-item: every item is answered under both conditions. Optional third arm — zero-shot CoT ("think step by step, then give a final answer") — is included if budget allows, prespecified here as a comparison arm for H1/H2 but not part of the primary contrast.

### 3.1 Items

Target: 40 items minimum — 24 entailed, 16 underdetermined — drawn from at least four item families (kinship/role riddles including surgeon-style bias items; scheduling/constraint puzzles; syllogistic/relational inference; short policy-hypothetical fact patterns). Item-generalisation is the point; more items beats more generations per item.

**Adjudication gate (before collection, blind to study hypotheses):** three independent experts per item receive the item text and a candidate target, and judge whether the target is uniquely entailed under explicitly listed assumptions, merely compatible, or whether an unintended alternative survives. Only items with unanimous "uniquely entailed" verdicts enter the entailed set; items enter the underdetermined set only if adjudicators unanimously agree no unique answer is entailed and can name the surviving alternatives (these become the gold set for calibration scoring). Items with split verdicts are excluded and logged. The predecessor's Sami riddle may be submitted to adjudication but is excluded from confirmatory analysis regardless of verdict, as its results are already known.

### 3.2 Generations and power

Ten generations per item×condition (40 items × 2 conditions × 10 = 800 calls per model). Analysis clusters by item; simulation-based power analysis (to be attached as an appendix before freezing, using predecessor variance estimates for the generation level and a conservative item-level ICC of 0.2–0.4) must show ≥80% power to detect a 10 pp calibration difference under H2. If it does not, increase items, not generations per item.

### 3.3 Models

Minimum panel: the predecessor model (GPT-5.6 Luna, low reasoning effort) for continuity, plus one other vendor family and one open-weight model, each at one fixed effort/temperature setting recorded in the frozen config. Confirmatory analysis pools models with model as a crossed random effect; per-model results are secondary.

### 3.4 Output budget (fixing the predecessor's confound)

Pilot 20 generations per condition on 5 items; set a single shared max-token cap at ≥1.5× the 99th-percentile pilot length of the *longer* condition, applied identically to both arms. Record finish reason for every call. Prespecified handling: truncated responses are scored as-is under all outcomes (no repair collection); truncation rates by condition are reported; if truncation exceeds 2% in either arm, all analyses are additionally run excluding truncated responses as a sensitivity. Condition-specific repair is prohibited.

## 4. Outcomes (all human-coded; definitions frozen with examples before collection)

Per response, coders record: (O1) **recognition** — identifies the adjudicated target (entailed items) or the adjudicated solution set (underdetermined items); (O2) **unqualified commitment** — selects exactly one final answer with no hedging language; (O3) **underdetermination flag** — explicitly states that the item does not entail a unique answer; (O4) **contradiction** — asserts something inconsistent with stated premises; (O5) **usable final answer** — exactly one extractable final answer present. The primary calibration outcome for H2 is derived mechanically: entailed item → O1 ∧ O2 ∧ ¬O4; underdetermined item → O3 ∧ ¬O4. No coder ever computes calibration directly; it is a deterministic function of the recorded codes, so the construct cannot drift during review.

## 5. Human verification

Two independent coders per response, blinded to condition, item type, and hypothesis direction, working from randomised, format-stripped-where-feasible response text (formal structure will partially unblind coders to condition; this is unavoidable and is mitigated by mechanical derivation of the primary outcome and by coding-manual examples in both formats). Report raw agreement and Cohen's κ per outcome code. Disagreements adjudicated by a third blinded coder; adjudication rate reported. Gold answers and the condition linkage never appear in coder-facing files.

## 6. Analysis

Primary: logistic mixed-effects model on the calibration outcome with fixed effects condition, item type, condition×item type; random intercepts for item and model, random condition slope by item. Estimand: marginal risk difference for condition, with cluster-robust (item-level) bootstrap 95% CI. Secondary hypotheses analysed identically on their outcomes, Holm-corrected. Sensitivity: per-model fits; excluding items flagged in any post-hoc adjudication challenge; excluding truncated responses. Equivalence/non-inferiority for H3 uses a −5 pp margin on the entailed-item commitment difference, 90% CI method matching the predecessor's conventions.

Missingness: API failures are retried up to 3 times at collection with logged attempts; responses absent after retries are recorded as missing, reported by condition, and excluded listwise (with a sensitivity treating missing as calibration-failure if missingness exceeds 1% in either arm or differs by >0.5 pp between arms).

## 7. What would disconfirm what

If H2 fails and H3's non-inferiority also fails on entailed items, the hedging tax is intrinsic to the scaffold, not an artefact of the predecessor's item — the scaffold genuinely trades accuracy-as-commitment for qualification, and the honest conclusion is that formalisation as implemented harms decisive correctness. If H2 succeeds and H3 holds, the predecessor's null is explained as outcome misspecification on an underdetermined item, and the auditability programme proceeds on firmer ground. Both branches are informative; this section exists so that neither can be reframed after results.

## 8. Freeze list (hash all before first API call)

Item texts and adjudication records; both (or three) prompts; model configs and decoding settings; the coding manual with worked examples; coder assignment and blinding procedure; this document including the power appendix; analysis code operating on a synthetic pilot dataset (dry-run committed with output); equivalence margins; the multiplicity scheme; the missingness and truncation rules. Any post-freeze amendment gets a dated addendum and applies only prospectively.
